ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, point a is at the upper left, connected by a wire to a vertical 1 kΩ resistor on the right; the lower terminal of this 1 kΩ resistor is connected to the upper node of a parallel branch. The parallel branch is drawn as a rectangular frame, the left branch is a 100 kΩ resistor, the right branch is a 1 kΩ resistor, and the upper and lower terminals of the two are respectively connected. The lower node of the parallel branch is then connected by a wire to point b at the lower left. Reasoning: Therefore the equivalent resistance between a and b is the upper 1 kΩ in series with the lower parallel network. By engineering approximation, when 100 kΩ and 1 kΩ are in parallel, because 100 kΩ is much larger than 1 kΩ, the parallel equivalent is approximately equal to the smaller 1 kΩ. Thus the total resistance is approximately 1 kΩ + 1 kΩ = 2 kΩ.
